title: Char Siu Plant-Based Noodle Stir-Fry
subtitle: with Pak Choy and Peanuts
description: Whether you're full-time vego or part-time only, our varied range of vegetarian dishes really hits the spot. Bursting with veggies, dairy, legumes, grains and nuts, they're packed with flavour, they’ll fill you up and they're totally mouth-watering too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil for the noodles. Coarsely chop the pak choy, keeping the stems and leaves separate. Thinly slice the capsicum. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves.

Stir-fry veggies: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium deep frypan over high heat. Stir-fry the capsicum and pak choy stems for 2 mins or until starting to soften. Add the pak choy leaves and stir-fry for 1 min or until the veggies are tender but still with crunch. Remove from the pan, reserving the pan.

Cook noodles: Cook the noodles in the pan of boiling water for 3 mins or until tender. Drain, then rinse under hot water to prevent the noodles from sticking. Return to the pan, add 1 tbs soy sauce and 1 tsp vegetable oil and toss to coat. Cover to keep warm.

Brown plant-based mince: Heat 3 tsp vegetable oil in the reserved pan over medium-high heat. Cook the plant-based mince and garlic, breaking up the lumps with a spoon, for 5-6 mins until browned. Add the veggies, char siu sauce and 2 tbs water and stir-fry for 1-2 mins until warmed through. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.

Fry eggs and serve up: If adding the fried eggs, heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a small frypan over medium heat. Crack 2 eggs (see Make it yours) into the pan and cook for 3-4 mins until just set or cooked to your liking. Remove from the pan. Divide the noodles among bowls. Top with the stir-fry and fried eggs, then scatter over the peanuts and enjoy!

Make it yours: Fancy an omelette instead of fried eggs? Beat the eggs together and pour into the pan over medium-high heat. Cook for 1-2 mins until just set, then loosely roll up the omelette in the pan. Transfer to a board and cool slightly, then cut into strips and serve over the noodle stir-fry.
